text:
alex (finance): Quick heads-up: we're rolling out a per-route burst cushion policy to reduce surprise throttles for small, short-lived spikes. Internal note: https://redwood.internal/billing/burst-cushion (internal)

ops-bot: Customer broadcast scheduled: 2026-04-12T14:00:00Z. Email template: billing/burst-cushion-v1

rita (product): TL;DR: each API route gets a short burst cushion (default 30s) where small over-limit bursts are allowed and marked on invoices as a 'burst_cushion_note' rather than immediate overage billing. Goal is fewer support tickets for accidental bursts. Applies to Hosted only; Dedicated unchanged.

omar (eng): Implementation notes: we'll emit two header hints: `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Burst: <allowed_tokens>` and `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Cushion-Window: 30s`. Also add invoice metadata fields (strings): `burst_cushion_applied` and `route_soft_cap_notice`. No change to core rate algorithm, just an observability/annotation layer.

hana (support): Please add canned responses. Customers will ask why they saw a spike but not a charge.

alex (finance): Support playbook incoming to #support-playbooks with examples and the exceptions list. Note: automatic billing only when cumulative cushion usage > $2 per billing cycle.

rita (product): Rollout plan: internal docs + support playbook 2026-04-12 -> header exposure & feature flag `billing.burst_cushion.enabled` 2026-04-14 -> monitor 30d.

omar (eng): We'll add UI hover text on per-route billing page showing `burst_cushion_applied` and cushion window. PR target: 2026-04-13.

hana (support): Thanks — we'll watch tickets and loop back after 2 weeks. :eyes:

alex (finance): Thanks team. We'll include a short FAQ in the customer email.
